snippet.text: - `npm run check` fails about twenty tests in a Claude Code session on the maintainer's Mac, in files that spawn processes, send signals or open sockets, with `EPERM`, `EBADF`, `ENOENT` on a stand-in binary, or a five-second timeout, and the same tests fail on a clean `origin/main` there. Cause: the session runs its commands inside Claude Code's own sandbox, which refuses those operations; it is not the load and not the change. A cloud session and CI have no such sandbox. From a host session, run the test files your change touches, say in the report that the whole gate cannot pass there and which files failed on `origin/main` too, and take CI on the exact head as the gate of record. Never read a background command's exit code as the gate's: on [pull request #634](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/634) the coordinator did, and started a round on a head whose gate had failed.

message.text: The new learning opens with a sentence of about 50 words. It runs from "`npm run check` fails about twenty tests" to "fail on a clean `origin/main` there" and puts the session, the files, four error signatures and the `origin/main` comparison in one sentence. Its fourth sentence, "From a host session, run the test files your change touches, ... and take CI on the exact head as the gate of record", is about 43 words and holds three instructions. This is one of two such breaches this change added to AGENTS.md. The other is at line 202, reported on its own.

properties.failureScenario: A builder reading Three reviews before ready has to untangle a 62-word sentence to find the rule that matters: Codex's review and the review of record never run again on fix commits. trigger.snippet:
After the first head, a fix pass gets a Melian round and nothing else. Codex's review and the review of record run once, on the first reviewed head, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-28, unless the coordinator's spot check voids a review of record, which then runs afresh on that same head: the three run together to build the record of which reviewer finds what, and Melian's recall is now enough to review the fixes alone.

Once the pull request merges, the coordinator has a Sonnet agent draft its defect list: each distinct finding a reviewer raised on the first reviewed head, who raised it, and the commit that answered it or the builder's reply disputing it. The draft is evidence, never the judgement. A fix does not show a finding was real, since a builder may fix noise to clear a status, so each finding is still adjudicated valid, noise or duplicate with `melian compare adjudicate`, as The comparison record says, and the shadow retirement rule counts what it counted before.

1. Codex's adversarial review, which the builder runs on its own branch at the first reviewed head, once, and posts with its findings in the pull request's report. It uses GPT-5.6 Sol at high effort by default. The design lens now runs on that model and effort, so it can replace this review; [the route decision](docs/decisions/2026-10-24-design-lens-on-codex-route.md) records why. Codex's review keeps running until it meets [the shadow retirement rule](docs/decisions/2026-10-06-shadow-retirement-merged-window.md), ten merged pull requests at recall 0.75 or better, and the maintainer retires it.

snippet.text: Melian reviews its own pull requests in rounds. After each fix pass, a Melian round runs: from the `melian round` workflow, which runs the default branch's build, or from the branch's own build on a host. A pull request that changes Melian's review code needs a round from its own build, since the default branch's build cannot exercise it; [the Actions rounds decision](decisions/2026-11-06-actions-rounds-run-default-branch-code.md) says why the workflow runs the default branch's. The workflow posts its comment and sets `melian/review` as the machine user `melian-status-bot`, whose token only the default branch's round can read, so a builder reads that login's comment and no other as the round's; [the decision](decisions/2026-11-08-round-comment-as-the-machine-user.md) says why. The run records the comment's body as a `melian/round-comment` status, which no one can edit, so a comment a writer edited after it posted fails the check, and so does one holding another comment's body; [the decision](decisions/2026-11-14-round-records-its-comment-body.md) says why. Codex's adversarial review and a review of record run beside the rounds. The loop ends when a round finds nothing above advisory apart from policy notices. `AGENTS.md` says who runs each part.

message.text: This change records a new decision: Codex's adversarial review and the review of record run once, on the first reviewed head, and fix passes get only a Melian round. It adds docs/decisions/2026-11-27-three-reviews-on-one-first-head.md and rewrites AGENTS.md, but leaves docs/design.md alone. Line 514 of design.md's review-loop section still says "Codex's adversarial review and a review of record run beside the rounds". Line 5 still says "Shadow reviewers remain until Melian reaches recall of at least 0.75", but the new decision's "What this retires" section calls taking both reviews off fix commits "a partial retirement of both, ruled by the maintainer outside the shadow retirement rule".

evidence.snippet:
Every pull request gets all three before it is marked ready, and gets them first on one head. The builder pushes its first head with the gate green, or with CI green on it where the gate cannot run, starts all three reviews on that commit together, and pushes no fix until all three have reported. It names that commit in its report as the first reviewed head. [The decision](docs/decisions/2026-11-27-three-reviews-on-one-first-head.md) says why: reviews run one after another, with fixes between, each saw different code, so nothing could say which reviewer missed what.

The design lens now runs on that model and effort, so it can replace this review; [the route decision](docs/decisions/2026-10-24-design-lens-on-codex-route.md) records why. Codex's review keeps running until it meets [the shadow retirement rule](docs/dec [cut at 2 KiB]

After that head, each fix pass gets a Melian round and nothing else. Codex's review and the review of record run once, on the first reviewed head. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session: "we've reached a level of recall that I'm satisfied with only using All 3 models for that first code review to build up our parity database. Following fixes, lets just use the melian review." The cost is accepted: no reviewer but Melian reads a fix commit, where Codex's review used to run after each fix pass and the review of record, running last, used to read most of them.

## What this retires

Taking Codex's review and the review of record off fix commits is a partial retirement of both, ruled by the maintainer outside [the shadow retirement rule](2026-10-06-shadow-retirement-merged-window.md). That rule's measured criterion, ten merged pull requests at recall 0.75 or better, still decides when Codex's review stops running on the first head.

Melian reviews its own pull requests in rounds. After each fix pass, a Melian round runs: from the `melian round` workflow, which runs the default branch's build, or from the branch's own build on a host. A pull request that changes Melian's review code needs a round from its own build, since the default branch's build cannot exercise it; [the Actions rounds decision](decisions/2026-11-06-actions-rounds-run-default-branch-code.md) says why the workflow runs the default branch's. The run records the comment's body as a `melian/round-comment` status, which no one can edit, so a comment a writer edited after it posted fails the check, and so does one holding another comment's body; [the decision](decisions/2026-11-14-round-records-its-comment-body.md) says why. Codex's adversarial review and a review of record run beside the rounds. The loop ends when a round finds nothing above advisory apart from policy notices. `AGENTS.md` says who runs each part.

Status: milestone 1, the local CLI loop, closed on 2026-10-04 with [the first publication](../packages/evals/runs/2026-10-04-first-publish.md). Milestone 2 makes Melian the review of record for its own repository. Shadow reviewers remain until Melian reaches recall of at least 0.75 against the shadows' adjudicated findings. Use the ten most recent eligible merged pull requests after 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z. Every merged pull request in this repository after that instant is eligible, whether its comparison exists or not. A missing record or pending adjudication in that window blocks retirement. Require at least one adjudicated valid in-scope distinct shadow finding; zero findings leave recall undefined and keep both shadows running. The maintainer alone may tighten the root policy. [The decision](decisions/2026-10-06-shadow-retirement-merged-window.md) closes that question.

properties.failureScenario: A contributor follows AGENTS.md's instruction to read docs/design.md before changing anything. Its review-loop section says Codex's review and the review of record run beside the rounds, and its status line says shadow reviewers remain until recall reaches 0.75. From that, the contributor expects both reviews to keep running on fix commits. They then run Codex's review after each fix pass, or treat a fix head that only Melian reviewed as short of the required reviews. Both contradict the new decision and AGENTS.md lines 200-206.
